 ----Petitioners  Versus 1. State Of Rajasthan, Through Pp 2. Mamta D/o Dharma, Aged About 18 Years, R/o Koldara,
 P.s. Kotada, Dist. Udaipur.
----Respondents For Petitioner(s) : Mr.Arvind Dadhich.

For Respondent(s) : Mr.Mukesh Trivedi, P.P.
 HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE KULDEEP MATHUR  ORDER 19/10/2023

This application for bail under Section 439 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the petitioners who have been arrested in connection with FIR No.131/2022 registered at Police Station Kotada, District Udaipur, for offences under Sections 366, 370, 343, 376(2)(N), 120-B IPC.

Learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that the allegation against the present petitioners is of abducting the prosecutrix with the help of co-accused person and taking her to Gujarat with the intent of sexually assaulting her.
Learned counsel submitted that the further allegation against the petitioners is that he sold the prosecutrix to co-accused Vijay.

Learned counsel [2023:RJ-JD:36121]
(2 of 3) [CRLMB-12263/2023] submitted that as a matter of fact, the prosecutrix voluntarily eloped with the co-accused Vijay and stayed with him in his paternal house out of her free will and volition.

Learned counsel submitted that the statements of the prosecutrix have been recorded before competent criminal court, wherein though she has stated that the petitioner had sold her to Vijay Dola @ Dhola vs State Of Rajasthan (2023:

1 but during cross- examination has admitted the factum of her marriage with co- accused Vijay and she having stayed in his paternal house with his family members.
Learned counsel submitted that it is highly improbable that if the prosecutrix was sold by the petitioners to the co-accused Vijay, then why would she run away with co- accused Vijay and marry him.
Learned counsel submitted that there are various contradictions in the court statements of the prosecutrix creating doubt about truthfulness of her statements before the court.

Lastly, learned counsel submitted that the petitioners are in judicial custody since 5.11.2022, challan has been filed, the statements of the prosecutrix have already been recorded before the competent criminal court, no apprehension of petitioners influencing the prosecutrix or other material witness has been shown by the prosecution and the trial of the case will take sufficiently long time, therefore,
the benefit of bail should be granted to the accused-petitioners.
Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor opposed the bail application.
Heard learned counsel for the petitioners and learned Public Prosecutor.
Perused the material available on record.

[2023:RJ-JD:36121] (3 of 3) [CRLMB-12263/2023] Having considered the rival submissions, facts and circumstances of the case so also the statements of the prosecutrix recorded before competent criminal court, this Court prima facie finds that there are large number of contradictions in her statements which definitely creates doubt about the correctness of the story narrated by her before competent criminal court.
Thus, without expressing any opinion on merits/demerits of the case, this Court is inclined to enlarge the petitioners on bail.

Accordingly, the bail application under Section 439 Cr.P.C. is allowed and it is ordered that the accused-petitioners- (i) Dola @ Dhola S/o Bada and (ii) Jagdish @ Jagla S/o Limba shall be enlarged on bail in connection with FIR No.131/2022 registered at Police Station Kotada, District Udaipur, provided each of them furnishes a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- with two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the learned trial Judge for their appearance before the court concerned on all the dates of hearing as and when called upon to do so.
It is however, made clear that findings recorded/observations made above are for limited purposes of adjudication of bail application.
The trial court shall not get prejudiced by the same.

(KULDEEP MATHUR),J 17-TarunGoyal/-
